key_insight: The paper argues that recurring agent control logic should be learned once as reusable harness code, rather than re-derived inside every prompt. This lets LLMs focus on task-specific reasoning while the harness handles stable execution decisions.
problem_solved: LLM agents often waste context and tokens by repeatedly reconstructing the same control strategy for related tasks. This work addresses the inefficiency and brittleness of strategy-free scaffolds that rely on the model to re-decide routine actions every time.
method: Introduce a "Growing Harness" training paradigm that converts failure feedback into executable control logic.
Start from a strategy-free scaffold that exposes fixed points where the harness can be improved and specialized.
Use repeated task failures to grow reusable agent behavior, reserving LLM calls for semantic, task-specific reasoning.
impact: For practitioners, this can reduce prompt length, token cost, and repeated reasoning overhead in multi-task agent systems. It also makes agent behavior more reusable, modular, and easier to optimize over time.

paper_title: Grow the Harness, Not the Context: From Strategy-Free Scaffolds to Reusable Specialist Agents
paper_authors: Laizhen Li, Jiarui Li, Juanjuan Zhao, Kejiang Ye, Ye Li
